0.long_answer: The deposits observed in age-related macular degeneration (AMD), particularly drusen, have been found to contain a protein that is more commonly associated with Alzheimer’s disease. This protein is the amyloid beta (Aβ) peptide. Amyloid beta is well known for its role in forming the extracellular plaques found in the brains of patients with Alzheimer’s disease. In the case of AMD, the presence of amyloid beta in drusen suggests that similar underlying processes such as complement activation and inflammation might contribute to disease progression in both AMD and Alzheimer’s disease.
